sentences.text: The applications are filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('Code' for short), for orders of pre-arrest bail.

2. The petitioners are the accused 2 and 3 in Crime No.644/2024 of the Kottayam East Police Station, Kottayam, which is registered against four accused persons for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Sections 409, 418, 420, 468 and 471 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. The crux of the prosecution allegation is that: the four accused persons, in furtherance of their common intention to make unlawful gain for themselves, and while the 1st accused was working as a Branch Manager of the defacto complainant Bank (Indus Ind Bank) ('Bank' in short) and the 2nd accused was the Back Office Executive and accused 3 and 4 were the 2024:KER:84332 Collecting Executives of the Bank, after collecting an amount of Rs.47,41,605/- from 13 customers failed to deposit the money in the customers' account by forging the receipts of the Bank, to make it appear that they had deposited the amounts.
Thus, the accused have committed the above offences.

4. Heard; Sri.T.N.Suresh, and Sri.S.Rajeev the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Smt.Seetha S., the learned Senior Public Prosecutor and Sri.K.Rajesh, the learned counsel appearing for the defacto complainant/intervenor.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are innocent of the accusations levelled against them.
There is no material to substantiate the petitioners' culpability in the crime.
The petitioners had deposited the entire amount received by them in the Bank.
The petitioners have not misappropriated any money of the Bank.
The petitioners' custodial interrogation is not necessary and no recovery 2024:KER:84332 is to be effected for the proper investigation in the crime.
The petitioners are ready to abide by any stringent condition that may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, the applications may be allowed.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned counsel appearing for the defacto complainant/intervenor, vehemently opposed the applications.
They submitted that there are incriminating materials to establish the petitioners involvement in the crime.

The 2nd accused, who was working as the Back Office Executive, had collected cash from the customers of the Bank, who had loan accounts, and instead of depositing the money in the loan accounts of the customers,
misappropriated the amount.

Similarly, the 3rd accused, who was working as a Collection Executive,
collected cash made bank transfers of the customers to his account and issued forged receipts to the Robin Varghese vs State Of Kerala on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71014488/
3 customers.

sentences.text: It is only when the customers approached the Bank for no-objection certificates, after paying the entire 2024:KER:84332 outstanding amount, that the defacto complainant came to learn that the accounts were not tallying and a misappropriation has taken place.

In an internal enquiry,
that was conducted, it was revealed that the accused have forged receipts and received cash and bank transfers to their personal accounts.
The accused persons have caused substantial loss to the Bank and its customers by collecting money and not remitting the same in the Bank.
The materials on record would prove that the petitioners have committed a serious economic offence.
The petitioners' custodial interrogation is necessary and recovery is to be effected for the proper investigation of the crime.
If the petitioners are granted an order of pre-arrest bail, it would hamper the investigation.
Therefore, the applications may be dismissed.

7. The prosecution allegation is that, the petitioners were working as Branch Manager, Back Office Executive and collection agents with the Bank had 2024:KER:84332 collected money from the customers of the Bank and misappropriated the amount by issuing forged receipts of the Bank to the customers.
It is only when the customers went to collect the NOCs, that the misappropriation and cheating was unearthed .

8. The petitioners had moved a similar application before the Court of Session, Kottayam, which was dismissed by Annexure-A5 order, finding that there are incriminating materials to substantiate their involvement in the crime.

9. On a consideration of the facts and the materials on record, and on comprehending the nature,
seriousness and gravity of the economic offences alleged against the petitioners, that there are prima facie materials to substantiate the petitioners' involvement in the crime, that the petitioners'
custodial interrogation is necessary and recovery is to be effected, I am not satisfied that the petitioners have made out any valid ground to invoke the discretionary jurisdiction of this 2024:KER:84332 Court under Section 438 of the Code.
The applications are meritless and are only to be dismissed.
In the result, the applications are dismissed.
